content: This is the discussion thread for #Lean Releases > v4.32.1.

Hi, thanks for the patch!
Is this bug limited to v4.32.0 or is it potentially backward compatible with previous versions too?

The bug exists in all prior versions, and the fix is easy to backport. If you run an older version of lean in a way that needs this fix and would dearly appreciate a backport and point release, please reach out to us

What exactly is the criteria for a soundness bug given that the PR says it is fixing a soundness bug, yet the discourse/release notes/pr convey that it's a soundness bug but doesn't affect comparator and the bug example is unable to be exported by lean4export. If a soundness bug is unable to be reproduced by the gold standard validation guidelines, why is it still worth fixing? There seems to be some nuance here.

It depends on which component you look at. The kernel itself, with its intended interfaces, is unsound with this bug. This is worth fixing, if only on principle.

The component “kernel wrapped in lean during interactive use” is also buggy, but already unsound in the presence of malicious meta code.

The component “kernel wrapped in comparator” is not buggy, because the bug cannot be triggered from the outside.

So you are right that it would have been defensible to not fix it (or fix it without stable releases). We decided to fix it in the stable kernel because we don't want the latest lean stable kernel (as its own component) to be unsound.

I would like to please ask a naive follow-up question. What exactly is the "kernel"? I would have thought that this was not a bug in the "kernel", since it does not survive proof export.

Put another way, I would revise @Claire Wang's question like this:

...the bug example is unable to be exported by lean4export. If a soundness bug is unable to be exported by lean4export, is it still a bug in the kernel?

Any insights would be appreciated. :pray:

The kernel does not even know what lean4export is, as it's a separately maintained data format. To make the kernel consume lean4export data, you have to add wrapper code. So the fact that lean4export happened to stop this bug because it didn't support fvars in opaques doesn't make it any less of a bug.

So to answer your question, the boundary of what is considered the "kernel" here, is the type checking code exposed purely through the C++ API. Any questions you can ask through that C++ API must be correctly answered.
Could one have by-hand constructed a proof in the format of an exported proof and triggered this bug in the type checking code?
No, the expression required to trigger the bug is syntactically unrepresentable in the export format
Thank you, @Jeremy Chen and @Henrik Böving, for your responses.
